steady.basis: Horizon revenue per earning IT MW and the actual modeled contract/spot revenue mix feed the shared steady-state DCF. Company running-cost margins and maintenance assumptions are retained. A 55% refresh reserve every four years plus 3% annual spares is a long-run house allowance, not compulsory retirement at a contract expiry. prepay.basis: ~70% of Q2-26 deals carried prepayments covering 50-60% of associated capex (Q2-26 letter) → 45% of GPU cost on contracted capacity; Microsoft prepaid $6.96bn of $17.39bn (40% of TCV, 20-F), credited through reduced monthly instalments from the start of each tranche → credited pro rata from month 1 over 2 years on mid-term deals (termQ 8, startQ 0); deferred revenue $5.98bn at 30-Jun-26 is the opening balance, credited over 20 quarters (Microsoft-weighted) Modeled future receipts retain the capex-based funding assumption; they are not secured financing. Inferred credits use modeled service start and contract expiry: first eight service quarters. Explicit opening-balance credits and special receipts retain their own dated schedules. Mixed future tranches allocate inferred credits by contractual IT MW; purchase capex remains scheduled if delivery slips.

finance.basis: debt 7% (first secured facility $775m at SOFR+250; converts 0.5-4.5% cash coupons with accreting principal), 16%/yr pool amortisation, $3bn cash floor; lenders advance 90% of GPUs and 65% of owned shell on contracted capacity, 50% on spot; 10% of capex from 2027 as policy equity at $132.15 (the 10 Nov 2026 mark; the last disclosed ATM sales averaged $223.60) plus the residual; eight convertible series at original principal $13.4bn, accreting to $15.7bn at maturity (post-Aug-26 exchange: 2029/2031 $0.175bn at $51.45; Sep-30/Sep-32 $3.16bn at $138.75; Mar-31/Mar-33 $4.34bn at $183.22/$180.31; Feb-30/Feb-34 $5.75bn at $313.46/$324.65; no capped calls) convert at the model 2030 price; restricted cash ~$1.1bn counted; fully diluted before converts 321.7m = 271.9m basic (30 Jun) + 15.8m Aug exchange + 21.1m NVIDIA pre-funded warrant + 6.2m RSUs + 6.7m options; non-core stakes (ClickHouse ~28%, Avride, Toloka, TripleTen) at the tracker mark of $5.8bn added to equity; opening cash $13.8bn = $8.04bn at 30 Jun (Q2-26 6-K) + $5.75bn August converts; restricted cash $1.056bn (cash-flow statement; $830m in other current assets); a $3.5bn Citi senior secured bridge (Term SOFR + 2.75% stepping to 3.50%, due 16 Oct 2027) was signed on 17 Oct 2026 — the amount drawn is undisclosed and a draw raises cash and debt equally, so it is not in the opening balances; discounted 4.14 years from 10 Nov 2026 to end-2030

power: contracted power guided for end-2026 · ~170 MW active at end-2025

facts: $14.2bn converts and secured − $13.8bn cash, pro forma Aug
notes: 5 GW contracted, >75% owned. Guidance stepped from >1 GW (Aug-25) to 5 GW (Aug-26) in a year. Owned greenfields: Mäntsälä and Lappeenranta (Finland, 455 MW), Independence MO (1.2 GW, groundbreaking May-26), Pennsylvania (1.2 GW, from 2027), Alabama. Leased: Vineland build-to-suit (Microsoft, 300 MW), Paris, Iceland, Kansas City, UK, Israel, Estonia, France, Spain.Q2-26 letter · 20-F · site releases

Connected lags contracted — and the 2026 guide is slipping. Management guides 800 MW–1 GW connected by end-2026 and more than 1 GW a year after. SemiAnalysis’s site work puts end-2026 at 573 MW and end-2027 at ~1.2 GW (cut from 1.7 GW): Vineland’s third tranche lands in December, Alabama’s first building and Béthune’s next phase in Q4-27, Pennsylvania in mid-2028. The page follows the later dates.Q2-26 call · SemiAnalysis 3Q26 update · AIB 8-K 30 Sep

Power is behind the meter at Vineland — and contested. Bloom Energy fuel cells (~250 MW guaranteed for 2026) and gas generators; New Jersey fined the landlord ~$1.07m on 22 September for 62 unpermitted engines with a permit deadline the landlord is challenging, and a 21 October Clean Air Act notice names Nebius. Phase 2, approved in August, lifts the campus to ~350 MW.Bloom partnership May-26 · NJDEP 22 Sep · notice of intent 21 Oct · Vineland Planning Board 18 Aug

~230k GPUs by December 2026 on ~490 MW energised — a quarter behind the company’s guide. Finland’s 75 MW hosts Europe’s first GB300 NVL72; Microsoft’s Vineland tranches are GB300.Q1-26 letter · Microsoft 6-K · model tranches
Five-year book life. Servers were depreciated over four years until Jan-26 (“conservative”), then five; the change cut H1-26 depreciation by $86m.20-F FY25 · Q2-26 6-K

Vera Rubin from early 2027. Meta’s $12bn dedicated capacity is one of the first large-scale Vera Rubin deployments, delivery H1-27; the $15bn backstop lets Nebius sell that capacity to others with Meta taking what is unsold.6-K 16 Mar 2026 · Q1-26 letter

Contract cohorts. Existing/inferred book keeps its original all-in rate until a disclosed or estimated expiry. Expiry ends signed coverage; continuation becomes an assumed renewal. New capacity uses one shared house curve.

Compare matching measures. Annualized earning contracted revenue divided by earning contracted IT MW measures contract yield. Total annualized revenue divided by all earning IT MW includes spot. Neither denominator should be paired with full energized-capacity ARR.

Evidence. Every tranche records price, commitment and expiry provenance. An inferred allocation is not a verified contract. New prices, zero software premium and 100% same-hardware renewal continuation are explicit assumptions.

Prepayments do the funding. ~70% of Q2-26 deals carried prepayments covering 50–60% of capex; >$9bn expected in 2026; Microsoft prepaid $6.96bn of $17.4bn. Deferred revenue $6.0bn at 30 June.Q2-26 letter · 20-F Note on Microsoft

Converts, then secured debt. Four convertible raises in 14 months — $1.0bn (Jun-25), $3.16bn (Sep-25), $4.34bn (Mar-26), $5.75bn (Aug-26); $13.4bn outstanding at original principal, accreting to $15.7bn, no capped calls — plus NVIDIA’s $2bn pre-funded warrant, a $1.15bn follow-on at $92.50 and $2.8bn of ATM at $223.60. The first secured GPU facility ($775m, SOFR+250) closed July-26; management expects “mid-single-digit billions” more against >$40bn of IG-backed contracts.6-Ks · 17 Jul 2026 release

The catch: prepayments and gearing follow signed contracts; the owned greenfields ($8m shell per MW) are built ahead of signing and most of the 2027 capacity is self-built. A $3.5bn 364-day Citi bridge was signed on 17 October. Unsigned capacity needs ~$19m of equity per MW, and new equity now prices near $132, not the $224 of the last ATM sales.funding stack above · 6-K 17 Oct 2026

Common calculation, different costs. The steady-state multiple is recomputed from horizon earned revenue per IT MW. Company margins, leased or owned shell costs, maintenance, tax and discount assumptions remain explicit.

Equipment life is separate. A contract expiry does not remove the GPUs or install a newer generation. Existing equipment renews at its own rate; the long-run maintenance reserve is a house assumption.
Reconciled value. Updated quarterly revenue passes through the existing debt, prepayment and dilution waterfall. The terminal multiple is recalculated from the displayed steady-state inputs.

Separate clocks. Pricing policy is dated 15 September 2026. The balance sheet is 30 June 2026 pro forma for the August converts — Q3 results arrive on 12 November 2026. Site timing and the market reference ($132.15, at which new equity is issued) are dated 10 November 2026.

arr.cap: Annualized earned revenue is split into existing book (including estimates), assumed renewals, assumed new contracts and spot. Full-capacity contracted run-rate is a separate measure.

footer.model: Shared pricing and contract-cohort model. Existing commitments, estimated coverage, same-hardware renewals and new business are distinguished. Pricing, expiry and continuity assumptions are exposed with their evidence. Company financing and capex retain the dated research snapshot.

capexBasis: GPUs + ancillaries per MW by vintage: $30m Blackwell (derived: 2026 capex guide $20-25bn against ~700 MW added; management: GPUs ~80% of total capex), +10% on 2027 orders, Rubin ~$38m, next-gen ~$45m; shell $8m per MW on owned campuses (management: data-centre build 18-20% of capex), none on co-location

market.units: USD millions per IT MW per year; all-in contracted services
market.tenorBasis: The initial new-business curve has no calibrated tenor premium or discount. Term controls the next renewal date. A five-year, 15% lower-price case is an explicit sensitivity, not a disclosed market spread.
market.generationBasis: The shared frontier curve is quoted per IT MW, with generation factors of 1 as an explicit house assumption. It is not a hardware productivity forecast. Existing equipment renews at its own all-in price; renewal does not install new GPUs.

renewal.basis: Base assumes the same hardware keeps earning at the original all-in rate and 100% contracted capacity renews. These are house assumptions, not commitments. Price and retention downside cases are shown.

spot.note: Shared realized spot assumptions inherited from the CoreWeave/Nebius model, not executable rate cards. Physical GPU density remains tranche-specific.

market.basis: One shared new-business curve using the existing Nebius 2027–30 house ladder ($18m/$19m/$20m/$21m per IT MW-year). Prices fix at modeled service commencement, not energisation. Current disclosures support improving pricing but do not establish these forward prices. Existing/inferred commitments retain their own rates through disclosed or estimated expiry. No quantified company software premium is assumed. The 2031 service-start price holds the 2030 level flat; it is a house extension, not a market quote.

limitations: Expiry quarters are estimates from modeled acceptance unless specifically marked disclosed.
An inferred existing-book allocation is not a verified customer commitment for that physical tranche.
Renewals do not retire or replace equipment. The long-run maintenance reserve is a separate house assumption.
Contract price by tenor is uncalibrated in the base case; the five-year discount is an explicit sensitivity.
Future prepayments and borrowing capacity are financing assumptions, not committed funding; customer credits follow modeled contract terms.
Delivery-delay tests retain the original capex purchase calendar. Fixed opening credit schedules remain unchanged.
Any prepayment balance without a credit calendar is deducted at face value at the horizon until its timing is sourced.
Forecast cash margin is 55%; normalized terminal margin is 55%.
